title: Midnight Telegram
description: A coded telegram preceded a diplomat's poisoning. Decode the message and catch the sender before they sail at dawn.
intro: A sealed envelope arrived at 11:47 PM. By midnight, Ambassador Cross was dead.

clue-1.title: Autopsy Summary
clue-1.content: Ambassador Cross died of cyanide at roughly 12:05 AM. A crumpled telegram was in his hand: 'QEB RFYN GBTBX' (Caesar cipher, shift unknown).

clue-2.title: Suspect: Victor Hale
clue-2.content: Trade attaché. Argued with Cross over shipping tariffs yesterday. Booked passage on the morning steamer.

clue-3.title: Cipher Scratch Pad
clue-3.content: Cross's notes test shifts on paper. Shift 3 yields: 'NBY OCVL YEQOU' — nonsense. Shift 1 is circled twice.

clue-4.title: Decoded Warning
clue-4.content: Applying Caesar shift 1 to the ciphertext yields: 'THE DEAD WALKS AT DAWN' — a threat timed for the ambassador's last morning.

clue-5.title: Dock Manifest
clue-5.content: Victor Hale's cabin trunk contains cyanide vials hidden in a false bottom. Ticket shows steamer departure 6 AM.

clue-6.title: Sender Identified
clue-6.content: Hale sent the coded warning after poisoning Cross, planning to flee at dawn. The cipher was meant to taunt, not save.

combinations.message: Shift 1 reveals the threat hidden in the telegram.

challenge.prompt: What does the telegram say (Caesar shift 1)?

combinations.message: Poison, coded threat, and dawn escape point to one attaché.

challenge.prompt: Who sent the telegram and poisoned Cross?

options.text: Victor Hale — cyanide in his trunk, steamer at dawn
The harbor master who logged the ship
Cross himself in a suicide note

suspects.name: Victor Hale
suspects.detail: Argument yesterday; steamer ticket; trunk searched at dock.

suspects.name: Ada Whitmore
suspects.detail: Transmitted the message. Claims she cannot read ciphers.

suspects.name: James Poole
suspects.detail: Delivered the telegram. No cyanide found on his person.

solution.explanation: Victor Hale poisoned Ambassador Cross, sent a Caesar-shift taunt, and planned to escape on the dawn steamer—stopped by the cyanide found in his trunk.
solution.redHerringNote: Ada transmitted the message but had no access to Cross's study or the poison.
